q: Our brute-force BFS for approximating the Hadamard gate through B_3 in the rho_{[2,1]} sector plateaus around Frobenius distance ~0.10 by length ~11 and does not improve monotonically after that. Is this an artifact of the BFS-with-pruning heuristic, or does the rho_{[2,1]} image have a systematic 'spectral gap' that limits what short braids can approximate, as opposed to the closure being dense?
basis: In our depth-15 BFS with pruning, the best Frobenius distance to Hadamard (under best global phase) oscillated between 0.10 and 0.24 rather than smoothly decreasing. Distance dropped from 2.0 (length 0) to 0.104 (length 11), then went back up to 0.20 (length 15) after the frontier hit the 400,000-state cap and had to be pruned to the 200,000 states closest to the target.
next_steps: (a) Implement a proper Solovay-Kitaev iterated approximation using length-N base atoms and verify the theoretical 1/l^2 scaling promised by Theorem 2.1 of FKW. (b) Repeat the search in the ρ_{[3,3]} sector (5-dim, 5 generators, more expressive) and see whether the plateau vanishes. (c) Numerically estimate the covering-radius exponent by fitting best_dist(l) ~ C * l^(-alpha) and compare against alpha = 2 (Solovay-Kitaev refined) and alpha = 1 (original Kitaev).

q: The paper's printed rho_{[2,1]}(sigma_2) matrix (Section 3) is not unitary under either natural literal reading of the typography. Which specific fix (sign flip, sqrt([3]) misprint, or a hidden basis-conjugation convention) recovers unitarity, and is the same typo present in the arXiv v1, the arXiv v2, and in the later published Bulletin AMS version of this paper?
basis: We tested both plausible sign conventions of the printed 2x2 matrix (readings A and B in fkw_replication.py) and both fail the unitarity check U^dagger U = I by O(1). Our independently constructed rho_{[2,1]}(sigma_2), built from the paper's own general formula (13)-(15), is unitary with the correct spectrum {-1, q}.
next_steps: (a) Diff arXiv/quant-ph/0001108 v1 vs v2 source (arXiv preserves LaTeX source) for that exact formula. (b) Compare against the Bulletin AMS 40(1) 2003 version. (c) Contact Zhenghan Wang (still active at Microsoft Station Q / UCSB) about a possible erratum. (d) Publish a two-line correction if confirmed.

q: The random-braid trace distribution in rho_{[2,1]} shows RMS deviation ~0.08 from the SU(2)/center Haar density (2/pi) * sqrt(1 - x^2) even at 50,000 samples with braid length uniform in [20, 60]. Is this a fixed-length equidistribution artifact, or evidence that the natural uniform-word probability measure on B_3 does not converge to Haar measure in this representation?
basis: We ran 50,000 random braid words of length uniform in [20, 60] and computed the empirical distribution of tr(U)/2 (projected to SU(2)/center). RMS deviation from the Haar density stayed at ~0.078 vs ~0.077 when going from 10,000 to 50,000 samples, indicating this is not sample noise but a real bias of the word measure.
next_steps: (a) Study which Markov chain / Plancherel-type measure on B_n provably equidistributes to Haar on the closure of rho(B_n). (b) Extend to word lengths 200-1000 and check whether the deviation vanishes as length grows. (c) Compare against the theoretical spectral gap of the random walk on rho(B_3) inside U(2)/Z; a nonzero gap should give exponential mixing in word length.

q: The paper embeds k qubits into V_{3k}^0, whose dimension grows as (a Fibonacci-related recurrence) rather than 2^k. What is the actual overhead ratio dim V_{3k}^0 / 2^k for small k (k = 1, 2, ..., 10), and how does the resulting 'qubit-smearing error probability' per gate compare to the O(epsilon^2) bound the paper cites for k = 1..10?
basis: Our C1 dimensions show dim V_6^0 = 5, so already for k=2 the modular-functor space is only 25 percent larger than 2^k = 4 - much tighter than a naive asymptotic argument would suggest.
next_steps: (a) Extend dim_V_n_ell(n, ell) to n = 3, 6, 9, ..., 30 and tabulate the overhead ratio. (b) Implement a full 2-qubit gate as an approximate braid on B_6, sample the induced probability of landing outside the k-qubit subspace, and measure the empirical smearing-error probability. (c) Compare against the paper's O(epsilon^2) with the same epsilon as the braid Frobenius distance. This closes a loop between the density theorem and the fault-tolerance analysis.

q: The Aharonov-Ben-Or fault-tolerance threshold cited in the paper (epsilon < 10^-6) predates modern surface-code / concatenated-code threshold analyses by ~15 years. Is CS5-with-braid-approximation-error still fault-tolerant under contemporary threshold analyses (Aliferis-Gottesman 2005, Aharonov-Kitaev-Preskill 2006, etc.), or does the 'systematic-not-random' nature of Solovay-Kitaev residual errors push the effective threshold materially lower for this specific topological model?
basis: The paper (Thm 2.2 discussion) explicitly notes the errors are 'not entirely random' due to the systematic biases of the Solovay-Kitaev approximation procedure, and treats them as 'malicious' to invoke AB.
next_steps: (a) Symbolic error-model construction: pick a fixed target gate g, compute the actual residual g - rho(b_L) after a length-L approximate braid, and check whether the residual has the special structure exploited by newer threshold proofs. (b) Numerically propagate this residual through a small concatenated code (e.g., Steane [[7,1,3]]) and measure the crossover epsilon. (c) Compare the crossover epsilon to the surface-code threshold (~1e-2) and to the paper's AB threshold (~1e-6).
